title: [Bug] MoE tuner writes config files the runtime never reads (int4_w4a16)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions.
- [x] Please use English.

### Describe the bug

For `int4_w4a16` MoE, the tuner writes its results to a filename the runtime never looks up, so tuning silently has no effect.

The runtime derives the config key from the down-projection shape — `fused_moe_triton_config.py:284`:

```python
E, _, N = w2_shape
```

The tuner applies an extra int4-only halving on top — `benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py:283-285`:

```python
N = shard_intermediate_size // 2
if use_int4_w4a16:
    N = N // 2
```

For `cyankiwi/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ-4bit` (E=256, `moe_intermediate_size` 512) the two disagree by exactly that factor of two:

```
tuner:   Start tuning over 400 configurations to create
         E=256,N=128,device_name=...,dtype=int4_w4a16.json

server:  Using default MoE kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal!
         Config file not found at .../E=256,N=256,device_name=...,dtype=int4_w4a16.json
```

The tuner runs to completion, reports success, and writes a file — but the server keeps using default tiles. Only `use_int4_w4a16` is affected, which is likely why it has gone unnoticed.

For reference, vLLM's `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py` computes `N = shard_intermediate_size // 2` with no second halving.

Suggested fix: drop the extra `if use_int4_w4a16: N = N // 2`.

This is not hardware-specific — the key mismatch is device-independent, though my environment happens to be ROCm.

### Reproduction

```bash
# 1. Tune an int4 MoE model — note the filename it announces
python3 benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton.py \
    --model cyankiwi/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ-4bit --dtype int4_w4a16 --batch-size 1 --tune
# -> "... to create E=256,N=128,device_name=...,dtype=int4_w4a16.json"

# 2. Serve the same model and note the filename it looks for
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path cyankiwi/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ-4bit
# -> "Config file not found at .../E=256,N=256,device_name=...,dtype=int4_w4a16.json"
```

### Environment

```
Python: 3.12.13
ROCM available: True
GPU 0: Radeon 8060S Graphics (gfx1151)
ROCM_HOME: /opt/rocm
HIPCC: HIP version: 7.13.26154-92b7431876
PyTorch: 2.13.0a0+rocm7.13.0a20260422
sglang: 0.0.0.dev1+g3f048c80b.d20260513
sglang-kernel: 0.4.2.post1
triton: 3.7.0+git6aa07328.rocm7.13.0a20260422
transformers: 5.6.0
numpy: 2.1.3
```
